title: Manual Pointer Arithmetic Optimization (Compiler-Bypassing Offsets)
pattern: Bypassing standard collection indexing or iterators in favor of manual raw pointer calculations (`.add()`, `.offset()`) under the assumption that it avoids bounds-checking overhead.
why_bad: It bypasses safe bounds checking, introducing severe memory unsafety risks. Furthermore, manual pointer arithmetic obscures the loop structure, preventing modern compiler optimization passes (such as loop vectorization) from optimizing the assembly.
detection: Use of `unsafe` blocks containing raw pointer additions (`.add()`, `.offset()`, `.sub()`) on slice or vector pointers.
counterexample: Low-level memory allocator implementations or custom OS kernel architectures where raw memory access is mandatory. `Context-dependent`.
